verdict: leakage cannot unprime the segment within a flight coast: shortest drain 367 s (debris-held seat, liquid, 25 C) vs coast <= 30 s ASSUMED; unpriming in 30 s needs >= ~1 g/s, i.e. a stuck-open seat (an effective hole ~0.1 mm2), which is a pintle failure, not leakage

acceptance_proposal.B-PNT-1 pintle seat: seat closed by the spiral spring alone (no servo torque), GN2 at 56 bar (Psat 25 C) upstream, chamber side at ambient, RT and after a 150 C soak of the head: <= 10 sccm GN2 (pressure decay or flowmeter on the chamber side); liquid N2O equivalent ~1 mg/s (same gap, viscous) -> > 8 h to unprime 44 cm3 and <= 0.6 g of N2O into the chamber over a 10 min hold (hard-start inventory criterion 20 g)
acceptance_proposal.B-PNT-1 stem seal: <= 1 sccm GN2 at 56 bar static, RT and 150 C (spring-energised PTFE class)
acceptance_proposal.B-MV-1 MV-P seat: ANSI/FCI 70-2 Class VI with GN2 at 56 bar and at 84.2 bar (MAWP), RT and 60 C (bay soak)
acceptance_proposal.CF-3: record P_feed (J602) and the segment TCs during every closed hold: the decay rate gives the in-situ leak (target: no measurable decay over 10 min while liquid remains, consistent with the B-PNT-1 number)
